name: Southern Marakwet
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Retired ISO code (2008), duplicate of Markweeta [enb] ('Talai is the name of a region'); no descriptive references for this entry.

sources.citation: Zwarts, Joost, Andrew Chelimo & Prisca Jerono. 2024. The reflexive in Kalenjin: its syntactic status and semantic functions. In ACAL in SoCAL (Language Science Press), 539-556.
Zwarts, Joost, Andrew Chelimo & Prisca Jerono. 2023. Two verbal plurals in Endo-Marakwet: a corpus study. Arusha Working Papers in African Linguistics 5(1): 51-66.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; fn.7: 'Tone marks nouns in nominative and verbs in the impersonal construction. In the Endo-Marakwet orthography, these are represented by : and /'. Useful bibliography (Rottland 1983 Marakwet dialects; Chelimo 2015; Zwarts 2004).

sources.citation: Kwambai, Lorna Jemwetich, Peter Nyansera Otieno & George Morara Anyona. 2022. Morphological adaptation of verb borrowings from Keiyo and Nandi languages on the vitality of Talai-Marakwet dialect. Research Journal in African Languages 3(2). Nairobi: Royallite Global.
sources.note: The only open work found on the Talai-Marakwet (TM) variety itself: verb morphology/tense prefixes and loan adaptation; no mention of stress, tone or prosody. Gives identity: 'Talai-Marakwet is a dialect of the Marakwet language... spoken in Kapsowar, Arror, Moiben/Kuserwo, Lelan, Sengwer and Cherang'any' and van Otterloo's (1979) split Talai-Marakwet / Sambirir Marakwet / Endo Marakwet.

sources.citation: Bible Translation and Literacy (BTL). 2018. Marakwet primer. Nairobi: BTL (43 pp., marakwetlanguage.com).
sources.note: Literacy primer; no statement on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Dimmendaal, Gerrit J. 2012. Metrical structures: a neglected property of Nilotic (and other African language families). Author's master copy PDF, Univ. Cologne. [already on file: ]
sources.note: Mentions Marakwet only for vowel length ('the long vowels of Marakwet are hardly longer than the short vowels of Kipsikiis'; fewer long-vowel sequences per word in Marakwet dialects); no Marakwet stress statement.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-162: retire [tle] Talai, merge into [enb] Markweeta (adopted 2008-01-14). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; identity only: 'There is no evidence to support the existence of Talai as the name of a distinct language. Talai is the name of a region... "Marakwet" is a cover term for Talai and Endo' -> merged into Markweeta [enb].

sources.citation: Zwarts, Joost. 2003. The Phonology of Endo: A Southern Nilotic Language of Kenya. Utrecht Institute of Linguistics OTS ms., 142 pp. (= Zwarts 2004, Muenchen: LINCOM Europa). CiteSeerX 10.1.1.129.5150 via Wayback Machine.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: TOZ Offsite Storage L.SOC.45.90.12.10 (59) (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Full phonology monograph of Endo (northern Marakwet). Chapter 8 'Tone' (pp.95-97): three underlying tonemes H, L, Falling; conditioned mid; downstep; F = HL. The words 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere in the 142 pp. (grep: only the gloss 'distress'); no statement on word stress, prominence or accent at all. Intro p.12-13 places Talai ('another Marakwet group, the Talai or Sambirir', 'the Talai of the highlands around Kapsowar') outside the Endo variety described.

sources.citation: marakwetlanguage.com (BTL Marakwet language project): Introduction, Marakwet Language History, Literacy/Primer pages.
sources.note: Nothing; history page reproduces Greenlee's 1982 survey letter naming Endo, Kew, Talai and Chesoi congregations.

sources.citation: Rottland, Franz. 1983. Marakwet dialects: synchronic and diachronic aspects. In B. E. Kipkorir, R. C. Soper & J. W. Ssennyonga (eds.), Kerio Valley: Past, Present and Future, 139-146. Nairobi: Institute of African Studies, University of Nairobi.

sources.note: The one published study specifically comparing the Marakwet dialects (Endo vs. Talai/Sambirir etc.); cited by Zwarts for the phonological isoglosses; may note prosodic differences. UoN erepository 11295/65862 has the volume record but only an abstract PDF.

sources.citation: van Otterloo, Roger & Karen van Otterloo. 1979. A Kalenjin dialect study. (Language Data, Africa Series 18.) Dallas/Nairobi: Summer Institute of Linguistics.

sources.note: SIL survey that distinguishes Talai-Marakwet (TM), Sambirir-Marakwet (SM) and Endo-Marakwet (EM) with phonological notes per dialect; the only description known to treat Talai as its own unit. SIL archive pages were Cloudflare-blocked from our machine.

sources.citation: Kisang', Philemon & Iver Larsen. n.d. Reading and writing Endo: a short introduction to the phonology of the Endo language. (BTL/SIL Kenya, unpublished); and Kwambai, Lorna J. (c. 2021) MA thesis on Talai-Marakwet verb borrowing, Kisii University (source of the 2022 article).

sources.note: Orthography-oriented phonology intro (Glottolog ref 151001) may state how tone/stress are (not) written; the Kisii MA thesis likely has a Talai-Marakwet phonology background section. Neither located online (Kenyan repositories KU/Moi unreachable, Kisii not indexed in CORE).

sources.note: Full modern grammar filed by Glottolog under Markweeta; Cherang'any/Sengwer is listed by Kwambai et al. 2022 among the Talai-Marakwet-speaking areas; its phonology chapter (tone, and any statement on stress) is the closest modern reference-grammar treatment to the southern/western Marakwet highlands.

sources.note: The TOC (fetched sources) proves a dedicated 'Druckakzent' (stress accent) paragraph in the Kalenjin description, which is built on Rottland's own field data from all Kalenjin dialects including Markweta (north '5n' and south); this is the only known first-hand stress statement whose scope includes southern Marakwet/Talai.
